# Function to summarize missing data for specified variables
# Count nulls for `monitor_vars`


dt_v <- BD_Hospitalar_Comunitario_30_resultados_joined

# Count nulls for `monitor_vars` (safe handling of non-character columns)
missing_summary <- tibble::tibble(variable = monitor_vars) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    present = variable %in% names(dt_v),
    n_total = ifelse(present, nrow(dt_v), NA_integer_),
    n_missing = purrr::map_int(variable, function(var) {
      if (!var %in% names(dt_v)) return(NA_integer_)
      vec <- dt_v[[var]]
      empty_str <- if (is.character(vec) || is.factor(vec)) vec == "" else rep(FALSE, length(vec))
      sum(is.na(vec) | empty_str, na.rm = TRUE)
    }),
    pct_missing = ifelse(!is.na(n_missing) & !is.na(n_total) & n_total > 0,
                         round(100 * n_missing / n_total, 2),
                         NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(pct_missing))

print(missing_summary)

```{r}
# Function to create and save a completeness bar chart (percent complete vs missing)
plot_completude <- function(df, var, dataset_name = "dataset") {
  if (!var %in% names(df)) return(NULL)
  vec <- df[[var]]
  total <- length(vec)
  n_missing <- sum(is.na(vec) | vec == "")
  n_complete <- total - n_missing
  comp_df <- tibble::tibble(
    status = c("complete", "missing"),
    n = c(n_complete, n_missing)
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(comp_df, ggplot2::aes(x = status, y = pct, fill = status)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(round(pct, 1), "%")), vjust = -0.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("complete" = "#2ca25f", "missing" = "#fb6a4a")) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = paste0(var, " completude (", dataset_name, ")"),
                  y = "Percent", x = NULL) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  fname <- file.path("plots/monitoria", paste0(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", paste0(dataset_name, "_", var)), "_completude.png"))
  ggplot2::ggsave(fname, plot = p, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 150)
  invisible(p)
}



# Generate completeness plots for the main surveillance dataset
for (v in monitor_vars) {
  try(plot_completude(dt_v, v, "BH,BC"), silent = TRUE)
}

generate_data_quality_report <- function(df,
                                         date_cols = NULL,
                                         id_cols = NULL,
                                         sample_size = 1000,
                                         na_threshold = 0.1,
                                         outlier_multiplier = 1.5,
                                         save_path = ".") {
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(df))
  n <- nrow(df)
  vars <- colnames(df)

  # 1) Normalize column names
  df <- df %>% janitor::clean_names()
  vars_clean <- colnames(df)

  # 2) Infer date columns if not provided
  if (is.null(date_cols)) {
    date_cols <- vars_clean[grepl("date|data|dt|time", vars_clean)]
  }

  # 3) Basic missingness and completeness
  missingness <- tibble(
    variable = vars_clean,
    type = sapply(df, class) %>% as.character(),
    n_missing = sapply(df, function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
    pct_missing = sapply(df, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
  ) %>%
    arrange(desc(pct_missing))

  # 4) Duplicates
  dup_rows <- df %>% duplicated() %>% sum()
  dup_report <- list(total_rows = n, duplicated_rows = dup_rows)

  # 5) Unique / cardinality
  cardinality <- tibble(
    variable = vars_clean,
    n_unique = sapply(df, function(x) length(unique(x)))
  ) %>% arrange(n_unique)

  # 6) Numeric summaries and outlier detection (IQR method)
  numeric_vars <- vars_clean[sapply(df, is.numeric)]
  numeric_summary <- map_dfr(numeric_vars, function(v) {
    x <- df[[v]]
    x_no_na <- x[!is.na(x)]
    if (length(x_no_na) == 0) return(tibble(variable = v))
    q <- quantile(x_no_na, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
    iqr <- q[4] - q[2]
    lower <- q[2] - outlier_multiplier * iqr
    upper <- q[4] + outlier_multiplier * iqr
    outliers <- sum(x_no_na < lower | x_no_na > upper)
    tibble(
      variable = v,
      min = q[1],
      p25 = q[2],
      median = q[3],
      p75 = q[4],
      max = q[5],
      mean = mean(x_no_na),
      sd = sd(x_no_na),
      n_outliers = outliers,
      pct_outliers = outliers / length(x_no_na)
    )
  })

  # 7) Categorical levels and unexpected values
  cat_vars <- vars_clean[sapply(df, function(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x))]
  cat_summary <- map_dfr(cat_vars, function(v) {
    x <- df[[v]]
    freqs <- as_tibble(table(x, useNA = "ifany"))
    freqs <- freqs %>% arrange(desc(n))
    top <- paste0(head(freqs$x, 5), collapse = "; ")
    tibble(variable = v, n_levels = length(unique(x)), top_values = top)
  })

  # 8) Date parsing and range checks
  date_checks <- NULL
  if (length(date_cols) > 0) {
    date_checks <- map_dfr(date_cols, function(col) {
      if (!col %in% vars_clean) return(tibble(variable = col, note = "not found"))
      x <- df[[col]]
      parsed <- suppressWarnings(parse_date_time(x, orders = c("Y-m-d","d/m/Y","d-m-Y","m/d/Y","Ymd","dmy","ymd"), exact = FALSE))
      n_parsed_na <- sum(is.na(parsed) & !is.na(x))
      n_all_na <- sum(is.na(parsed))
      date_range <- if (all(is.na(parsed))) tibble(min = NA, max = NA) else tibble(min = min(parsed, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(parsed, na.rm = TRUE))
      tibble(variable = col,
             parsed_non_na = sum(!is.na(parsed)),
             parsed_failed = n_parsed_na,
             parsed_all_na = n_all_na,
             min_date = date_range$min,
             max_date = date_range$max)
    })
  }

  # 9) ID uniqueness checks
  id_checks <- NULL
  if (!is.null(id_cols)) {
    id_present <- id_cols[id_cols %in% vars_clean]
    if (length(id_present) > 0) {
      id_checks <- map_dfr(id_present, function(idc) {
        total <- nrow(df)
        n_unique <- n_distinct(df[[idc]])
        pct_unique <- n_unique / total
        duplicated <- total - n_unique
        tibble(variable = idc, n_unique = n_unique, duplicated = duplicated, pct_unique = pct_unique)
      })
    }
  }

  # 10) Threshold-based flags
  flag_na <- missingness %>% filter(pct_missing >= na_threshold) %>% pull(variable)

  # 11) Assemble report
  report <- list(
    generated_at = Sys.time(),
    total_rows = n,
    missingness = missingness,
    duplicates = dup_report,
    cardinality = cardinality,
    numeric_summary = numeric_summary,
    categorical_summary = cat_summary,
    date_checks = date_checks,
    id_checks = id_checks,
    na_flags = flag_na
  )

  # 12) Save outputs
  date_tag <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")
  csv_path <- file.path(save_path, paste0("dq_missingness_", date_tag, ".csv"))
  readr::write_csv(missingness, csv_path)
  saveRDS(report, file = file.path(save_path, paste0("dq_report_", date_tag, ".rds")))

  # 13) Print short summary
  cat("Data quality report generated:", as.character(report$generated_at), "\n")
  cat("Rows:", report$total_rows, "- Variables:", length(vars_clean), "\n")
  cat("Duplicated rows:", report$duplicates$duplicated_rows, "\n")
  if (length(flag_na) > 0) {
    cat("Variables above NA threshold (", na_threshold, "):", paste(flag_na, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("No variables exceed NA threshold.\n")
  }

  invisible(report)
}

# Example usage:
 report <- generate_data_quality_report(BD_VH_VC_VA_Intermidiaria_15_resultados_joined,
                                        date_cols = c("dados_demograficos_date2"),
                                        id_cols = c("id_paciente"),
                                        save_path = "reports")

  "Codigo_do_tecnico",
  "Dados_demograficos:DATE2",
  "Dados_demograficos:codigo_paciente",
  "Dados_demograficos:idade2",
  "Dados_demograficos:provincia_de_residencia",

  "meta:instanceID"

# Calculate completeness for each variable
calculate_completeness <- function(df, variables) {
  
  results <- data.frame(
    Variable = character(),
    Complete = numeric(),
    Missing = numeric(),
    Total = numeric(),
    Completeness_Pct = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (var in variables) {
    if (var %in% names(df)) {
      total <- nrow(df)
      
      # Handle different data types safely
      col_data <- df[[var]]
      
      # Convert to character to avoid date parsing issues
      if (inherits(col_data, c("POSIXct", "POSIXt", "Date"))) {
        col_data <- as.character(col_data)
      }
      
      # Count missing values
      missing <- sum(is.na(col_data) | 
                     (is.character(col_data) & (col_data == "" | col_data == " " | trimws(col_data) == "")))
      
      complete <- total - missing
      pct <- (complete / total) * 100
      
      results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
        Variable = var,
        Complete = complete,
        Missing = missing,
        Total = total,
        Completeness_Pct = pct
      ))
    } else {
      warning(paste("Variable not found:", var))
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# Calculate completeness
quality_summary <- calculate_completeness(resultado_testagem_20, vars_to_monitor)

# Prepare data for visualization
quality_long <- quality_summary %>%
  select(Variable, Complete, Missing) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Complete, Missing), 
               names_to = "Status", 
               values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(Variable = gsub(":", "\n", Variable))  # Line break for readability

# Chart 1: Stacked Bar Chart - Completed vs Missing
p1 <- ggplot(quality_long, aes(x = reorder(Variable, -Count), y = Count, fill = Status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Complete" = "#2ecc71", "Missing" = "#e74c3c")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Data Quality Overview: Complete vs Missing Data",
    subtitle = paste("Total Records:", unique(quality_summary$Total)),
    x = "Variables",
    y = "Number of Records",
    fill = "Status"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

print(p1)

# Chart 2: Completeness Percentage
p2 <- ggplot(quality_summary, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Completeness_Pct), 
                                   y = Completeness_Pct)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", aes(fill = Completeness_Pct)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Completeness_Pct, 1), "%")), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#e74c3c", mid = "#f39c12", high = "#2ecc71",
                       midpoint = 50, limits = c(0, 100)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 110), labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Data Completeness Rate by Variable",
    x = "Variables",
    y = "Completeness (%)",
    fill = "Completeness %"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p2)

# Chart 3: Summary Statistics Table
quality_summary_display <- quality_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Completeness_Pct = round(Completeness_Pct, 2),
    Variable = gsub(":", ": ", Variable)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Completeness_Pct))

print("Data Quality Summary Table:")
print(quality_summary_display)

# Identify critical issues (< 80% complete)
critical_vars <- quality_summary %>%
  filter(Completeness_Pct < 80) %>%
  arrange(Completeness_Pct)

if (nrow(critical_vars) > 0) {
  cat("\n⚠️ ALERT: Variables with <80% completeness:\n")
  print(critical_vars %>% select(Variable, Completeness_Pct, Missing))
} else {
  cat("\n✓ All variables have ≥80% completeness\n")
}

# Overall data quality score
overall_score <- mean(quality_summary$Completeness_Pct)
cat("\n📊 Overall Data Quality Score:", round(overall_score, 2), "%\n")

colnames(raw) <- tolower(colnames(raw))


#create epiweek by DATE2
raw <-raw %>% mutate(week = lubridate::week(parse_date_time(`dados_demograficos:date2`, orders = c("Ymd","Y-m-d","dmY","d/m/Y","mdY","m/d/Y","Ymd HMS","dmY HMS"))))

#============================================================#
# FUNÇÃO PARA ENCONTRAR COLUNAS IMPORTANTES
#============================================================#
find_col <- function(possible_names) {
  found <- intersect(possible_names, colnames(raw))
  if (length(found) == 0) return(NA_character_) else return(found[1])
}

col_id       <- find_col(c("codigo_paciente","codigo paciente","codigo","id","sample","codigo_pac"))
col_week     <- find_col(c("week"))
col_influenza<- find_col(c("TIFOIDE:Resultado_de_Influenza"))
col_sars     <- find_col(c("group_jz9ln80:SARSCov2"))
col_date     <- find_col(c("dados_demograficos:date2"))

if (any(is.na(c(col_id, col_week, col_influenza, col_sars)))) {
  stop("❌ ERROR: Missing required columns (codigo_paciente, Week, Influenza, SARS-CoV-2)")
}

#====================#
# RENOMEAR COLUNAS
#====================#
df <- raw %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    codigo_paciente = !!sym(col_id),
    Week = !!sym(col_week),
    Influenza = !!sym(col_influenza),
    SARS_CoV_2 = !!sym(col_sars)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    codigo_paciente = as.character(codigo_paciente),
    Week = as.character(Week),
    Influenza = as.character(Influenza),
    SARS_CoV_2 = as.character(SARS_CoV_2)
  )

#====================#
# PADRONIZAR SEMANA
#====================#
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Week = str_trim(Week),
    Week = str_replace_all(Week, "^0+", ""),
    Week = ifelse(Week == "", NA, Week),
    Week_num = as.integer(Week)  # transforma string/número da semana em inteiro
  )

#====================#
# EXTRAR ANO DA COLUNA DE DATA
#====================#
if (!is.na(col_date) && col_date %in% colnames(df)) {
  df$data_evento <- suppressWarnings(
    parse_date_time(df[[col_date]], orders = c("ymd","dmy","mdy","Ymd","dmY"))
  ) %>% as.Date()
  df$ano <- year(df$data_evento)
} else {
  df$ano <- year(Sys.Date())
}

#====================#
# CRIAR COLUNA ANO_SEMANA (ex: 2024_W43)
#====================#
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Ano_Semana = paste0(
      ano, "_W", stringr::str_pad(Week_num, width = 2, pad = "0", side = "left")
    )
  )

#====================#
# CRIAR FATOR ORDENADO
#====================#
week_levels <- df %>%
  distinct(Ano_Semana) %>%
  arrange(Ano_Semana) %>%
  pull(Ano_Semana)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Ano_Semana_f = factor(Ano_Semana, levels = week_levels)
  )

#====================#
# DEFINIR TIPO DE VIGILÂNCIA
#====================#
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    codigo_trim = str_trim(toupper(coalesce(codigo_paciente, ""))),
    setting = case_when(
      str_detect(codigo_trim, "^[IL]DSW") ~ "Wastewater",
      str_detect(codigo_trim, "^IDSC")    ~ "Community",
      str_detect(codigo_trim, "^IDS")     ~ "Health Care Facility",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(setting %in% c("Community", "Health Care Facility", "Wastewater"))

#====================#
# LIMPAR RESULTADOS
#====================#
clean_result <- function(x) {
  x2 <- tolower(str_trim(coalesce(x, "")))
  x2[x2 %in% c("", "-", "na", "n/a")] <- NA_character_
  return(x2)
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    influenza_clean = clean_result(Influenza),
    sars_clean      = clean_result(SARS_CoV_2)
  )

#====================#
# FUNÇÃO – CALCULAR POSITIVIDADE
#====================#

compute_positivity <- function(df, result_col) {
  
  # Garantir que coluna Ano_Semana_f existe
  if (!"Ano_Semana_f" %in% colnames(df)) {
    stop("❌ A coluna 'Ano_Semana_f' não existe. Crie-a antes de calcular positividade.")
  }
  
  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[result_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(setting, Ano_Semana_f, ano, Week_num) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      tests = dplyr::n(),
      positives = sum(.data[[result_col]] == "positivo", na.rm = TRUE),
      positivity = ifelse(tests > 0, 100 * positives / tests, 0),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}



influenza_pos <- compute_positivity(df, "influenza_clean")
sars_pos      <- compute_positivity(df, "sars_clean")


#====================#
# REGRA WASTEWATER
#====================#
influenza_pos <- influenza_pos %>%
  mutate(positivity = ifelse(setting=="Wastewater" & positives>0, 100, positivity))

sars_pos <- sars_pos %>%
  mutate(positivity = ifelse(setting=="Wastewater" & positives>0, 100, positivity))

#====================#
# FUNÇÃO – PLOTAR
#====================#
plot_by_pathogen <- function(pos_df, title_text, out_file) {
  
  pos_df <- pos_df %>%
    arrange(setting, Week_num)
  
  colors <- c(
    "Community" = "#f39c12",
    "Health Care Facility" = "#7fc8ff",
    "Wastewater" = "#c41f1f"
  )
  
  p <- ggplot(pos_df, aes(x = Ano_Semana_f, y = positivity, color = setting)) +
    geom_line(group = 1, size = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(setting)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,100)) +
    labs(
      x = "Epidemiological Week / Year",
      y = "Positivity Rate (%)",
      title = title_text
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  ggsave(out_file, plot = p, dpi = 300, width = 18, height = 9)
  message("Saved plot: ", out_file)
  
  return(p)
}

#====================#
# PLOTAR GRÁFICOS
#====================#
plot_by_pathogen(influenza_pos, "Influenza Positivity Surveillance", "Influenza_Pos.png")
plot_by_pathogen(sars_pos, "SARS-CoV-2 Positivity Surveillance", "SARS-CoV-2_Pos.png")

#====================#
# EXPORTAÇÃO PARA DASHBOARD
#====================#
influenza_pos_v <- influenza_pos %>% mutate(tipo="Influenza")
sars_pos_v      <- sars_pos %>% mutate(tipo="SARS-CoV-2")

combined_pos_sars_inf <- bind_rows(influenza_pos_v, sars_pos_v)

combined_pos_sars_inf$setting <- plyr::revalue(
  combined_pos_sars_inf$setting,
  c("Community" = "COMUNIDADE",
    "Health Care Facility" = "HOSPITAL",
    "Wastewater" = "AGUAS RESIDUAIS")
)

# mostrar os graficos gerados de positividade



write_csv(combined_pos_sars_inf, "Sars_Influenza_Positivity_Data.csv")

message("All done ✅")
message("Output files saved in: ", getwd())




```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
